2. Heard Mr. S. Bahadur, learned counsel for the Petitioner, Mr. S.Nayak, learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State and Mr. P.K. Parhi, learned DSGI along with Mr. J. Nayak, learned CGC appearing for Opposite Party No.4.
3.

The petitioner has filed this Writ Petition seeking following relief:-
"Issue rule Nisi calling upon the Opposite Parties as to why the suit fand shall not be acquired and/or without acquiring the suit land the Opp Parties may be prohibited from interfering/reserving the suit land for S.E.Railway and to pay compensation of Rs 10 Lakhs for forcibly cutting and removing the trees, if the Opp. parties do not show cause or shown insufficient cause, issue a writ in the nature of mandamus or any other appropriate writ/writs, order/orders, direction/directions in directing the Opp Parties to acquired the suit land and/or without acquiring the suit land the Opp.
Parties may be prohibited from interfering/reserving the suit land for S.E.Railway and a further direction be made to the Opp. Parties to pay compensation of Rs.10 Lakhs for forcibly cutting and removing the trees."
4.

Mr. Bahadur, learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner contended that without issuing notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act and without paying any compensation to the Petitioner, the land of the Petitioner has been acquired and the trees standing thereon have been cut and removed.
Therefore, he has approached this Court in the present writ petition.

sentences.text: 5. Mr. S.Nayak, learned Additional Standing Counsel contended that if the Petitioner alleged that his land has been acquired without any notification, in that event, the Petitioner has got alternative remedy other than approaching this Court in the present writ petition.

6. Mr. P.K. Parhi, learned DSGI contended that the land has been acquired by the State and, as such,
the Central Government has no role to play so far as the relief sought by the Petitioner in the present writ petition.

7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and after going through the records, this Court finds that the Petitioner claims to be the owner of the land appertaining to Khata No.61/90, Plot No.617/905, area Ac. 0.950 decimal, Kissam: Goda-II of Mouza Kuisira, Tahasil: Hemgir in the district of Sundargarh, and that his land has been acquired for the purpose of South Eastern Railway without any notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act nor has he been paid any compensation.
On the other hand, the Petitioner has been dispossessed from the land, which was under his occupation.

But fact remains, if the allegation of the Petitioner is taken into consideration,
the private land of the Petitioner having been acquired, without any notification and without paying any compensation, in that case, such acquisition may be bad in law.

8. In view of such position, since the personal land of the Petitioner has been acquired and there is dispute with regard to receipt of compensation and delivery of possession thereof in favour of South Eastern Railway by the State Government, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the same,
rather permits the Petitioner to pursue his remedy in accordance with law before the appropriate forum.

9. With that liberty, the writ petition stands disposed of.
 (DR. B.R. SARANGI  JUDGE  (G.SATAPATHY)
